home.pageDescription: ApiVerCon (Api Version Control System) keeps a register of third-party API documentation - OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Postman and GraphQL - with every version archived, breaking changes spotted, alerts for your team and search across all endpoints.

hero.title: ApiVerCon
hero.tagline: Version control for the APIs you depend on but do not own — every version archived, every change graded, your whole team alerted.
hero.description: Link to a specification or upload it — OpenAPI/Swagger, AsyncAPI, a Postman collection or a GraphQL schema. ApiVerCon watches for new versions on its own, archives every one, compares it with the previous and tells your team what broke. Documentation belongs to your team, groups into collections and integrations, and carries your notes in a knowledge base.

formats.heading: One register for every kind of API contract
formats.text: The format is recognised from the content. Where a format has no version number, ApiVerCon derives one from the structure.

register.title: Register
register.text: Link to a specification or upload a file. A link can be added later, and checked daily, weekly, monthly or on demand.

watch.title: Watch and archive
watch.text: Every new version is stored and the old one archived. A specification that changes without a new version number is caught too.

compare.title: Compare and alert
compare.text: The new version is compared with the one before it: breaking, risky and harmless changes are counted, and your team hears about it by e-mail, bell, banner, Slack or webhook.

features.heading: Everything ApiVerCon gives you
features.subheading: Hover a card to see more detail.

registry.title: Central registry with version history
registry.summary: One place for the API documentation of every third-party app you work with — with every version archived.
registry.detail: Register a doc from a URL, or upload a file directly. Every new version is archived automatically, so you can look back even after it's no longer officially available.

formats.title: OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Postman, GraphQL
formats.summary: Not just REST: event-driven APIs, Postman collections and GraphQL schemas are first-class citizens.
formats.detail: Each format is recognised automatically. Swagger UI and ReDoc show OpenAPI; the other kinds open as a filterable list of endpoints. GraphQL schemas and Postman collections get a version derived from their structure.

notifications.title: Automatic rechecks and alerts
notifications.summary: Set a recheck period and let new versions get caught automatically.
notifications.detail: A daily, weekly or monthly check compares the specification's version, and archives a new one when it changes. We send an email, an in-app notification, and a banner right on the documentation page.

contentChanges.title: Silent changes don't slip through
contentChanges.summary: A spec changed without a new version number? ApiVerCon notices and keeps both.
contentChanges.detail: When the version stays the same, the content is compared by a fingerprint that ignores formatting and key order. A real change becomes a new entry marked "content changed" and the old one is archived. Switch it off for a spec that changes on every check.

breakingChanges.title: Breaking changes at a glance
breakingChanges.summary: Every new version is compared with the previous one, and the changes are graded.
breakingChanges.detail: Breaking, potentially risky and harmless — judged from the user's side: what a client sends and what it receives are weighed differently. Counts appear in the history, e-mails and notifications, and a "Changes" page lists each one in your language.

endpointSearch.title: Search across every endpoint
endpointSearch.summary: Find any endpoint in all the documentation you may see.
endpointSearch.detail: Search by path, name, method, description or tag — diacritics and case ignored. Narrow it by method or kind of document. It works for REST operations, GraphQL fields, AsyncAPI channels and Postman requests alike.

collections.title: Collections for related APIs
collections.summary: Group documentation that belongs together into one shared collection.
collections.detail: Whether it's a set of microservices or competing providers of the same service, a collection keeps their documentation together — with its own knowledge base.

integrations.title: Integrations that feel every change
integrations.summary: Combine collections and standalone docs into one view for a project — and hear when any of them changes.
integrations.detail: An integration can use a whole collection plus standalone docs on top. Members of its team are alerted about changes even if they never subscribed, and the integration's page shows what each document changed. Its knowledge base includes the knowledge base of every collection it uses.

pins.title: Pin the version you built against
pins.summary: See how far behind your integration is, and what has changed since.
pins.detail: Pin the current version of a document in one click, or pick an earlier one from its history. The integration then says "Built against 1.2.0", how many newer versions there are and what broke since.

knowledgeBase.title: A knowledge base for your team
knowledgeBase.summary: Notes, procedures and how-tos, kept right next to the docs you use.
knowledgeBase.detail: Create your own pages of team know-how for any collection or integration. Editing a collection's knowledge base is reflected in every integration that includes it — no need to write the same thing twice.

sharing.title: Team-owned, optionally public
sharing.summary: Documentation and collections belong to a team from day one — and can be opened up to everyone.
sharing.detail: The author can mark documentation or a collection as public, so anyone in the app can browse it, subscribe to update notifications and write to the author — even without being on the owning team.

webhooks.title: Slack and webhooks
webhooks.summary: Post new-version news where your team already works.
webhooks.detail: Send a message to Slack or to your own endpoint when a document your team owns or depends on gets a new version. Webhook calls are signed with HMAC-SHA256, can be limited to breaking changes and show how the last delivery went.

microservices.title: A team with several microservices
microservices.text: Five microservices' API docs get rechecked automatically every week. The moment any of their specs bumps its version, the whole team gets an email and an in-app notification — nobody has to check by hand.

paymentProviders.title: Comparing payment providers
paymentProviders.text: You add three payment gateways' documentation into one "Payments" collection. Anyone on the team can then find them in one place, instead of digging up links from chat or old notes.

integrationScoped.title: A new feature, precisely scoped
integrationScoped.text: For a new feature, you create an integration from exactly the APIs it depends on — one collection plus one extra standalone doc. You add the team's notes on rate limits and auth quirks straight to the integration's knowledge base.

breakingBeforeDeploy.title: A breaking change caught before release
breakingBeforeDeploy.text: A payment provider publishes a new version of its spec. Before your next deploy, ApiVerCon's e-mail already says "1 breaking change" — a required field was added to a request — and the Changes page points at the exact operation.

pinnedVersion.title: Knowing how far behind you are
pinnedVersion.text: Your integration is pinned to version 2.3. One look at its page shows the provider is two versions ahead and what changed in between — you plan the upgrade instead of finding out in production.

findEndpoint.title: Where was that endpoint?
findEndpoint.text: Instead of opening five documentations, you search "invoices" once and get every matching endpoint — across REST, GraphQL and AsyncAPI — with the document and version it lives in.

trust.heading: Your documentation, your control
trust.text: Private documentation is visible only to your team; only what you make public is open to everyone. No tracking, no ads, no analytics — just the technical storage needed to keep you signed in.
